Sport is more than the score.

Diverax is a podcast about sports culture. Beyond results and stats, we talk about how sport carries a place's memory, identity and community — bringing the world's sports culture to Taiwan, and Taiwan's to the world.

01

Who I am

I'm Alexander Hung, a Taiwanese, self-employed sports culture practitioner. I've followed and studied MLB since 2006, spent two years teaching English inside Taiwanese baseball, and once travelled alone to Argentina for a month to watch Messi play and to walk into La Bombonera and El Monumental. Diverax follows two threads: the international faces of Taiwanese baseball (foreign players, interpreters, scouts, Taiwanese players abroad) and the football cultures of South America.

Teams & players
Two years as English teacher for the Taiwan Beer baseball team at National Taiwan Sport University, teaching current pro players including Cheng Hao-chun and Lin Hui-sheng
Grassroots football
Convener of TWFA (Taiwan Football/Futsal Academy), National Taiwan Sport University's grassroots football outreach program
Baseball tech & hosting
Member of BasePara's baseball-technology team and event host at the 2020 Taiwan Sports Industry Expo
Writing
Contributor to The Crossing (CommonWealth Magazine) and The News Lens; long-form essays on Substack, Diverax by Alexander Hung
Speaking & teaching
Speaker in Hsuan Chuang University's 2026 sport and life education lecture series ("Meeting Yourself 10,000 km Away"); teaches a podcast marketing course

Questions I've actually asked

From EP.4, Venezuelan baseball with Josue Aldama. More than results and stats, I'm curious about the people, places and memories behind the sport.

  1. Q1When Venezuela won the championship, what was the first thought that came to your mind?
  2. Q2Venezuela has gone through incredibly difficult times. When millions of people were screaming for the same thing after this win, why did it feel like more than just sport?
  3. Q3When the world looks at Venezuela, it often sees only struggle and division. But when a kid hits a rubber ball into the sky over Caracas, what can the world's hardships never take away from Venezuela?Josue's first words in reply: "What a good question, friend."

I've also interviewed

Before Diverax, I also interviewed people across Taiwanese sport, media and government.

03

What you get

A conversation you haven't had

Before we record, I go through your past interviews, so we skip the questions you've answered many times and get to the side of your story people rarely hear.

Assets ready to share

When the episode goes live, you get 9:16 clips, quote cards and a caption you can post as is.

Listeners beyond Taiwan

Episodes are recorded in Mandarin, English or Spanish, with bilingual subtitles on clips, so your story reaches people outside your usual circle.

People worth knowing

Diverax guests span baseball, football, photography and South America. If someone would be a good fit for you, I'm happy to introduce you.

Yours to use

Share the episode, clips and quote cards freely on your own social channels, website or newsletter. No need to ask first.

04

Format & time

BEFORE
No prep needed

No script to write. Within 24 hours of confirming, I send you one page: the core question of the episode, three or four broad directions (not a full script), and how to join. A 15-minute unrecorded chat beforehand is optional.

RECORDING
45–70 min

Online via Riverside: all you need is headphones and a browser. Click a link, nothing to install. In person in Taipei or Hsinchu also works. Mandarin, English or Spanish, on your schedule, in any time zone.

AFTER
Live in 2–3 weeks

The episode goes live about 2–3 weeks after recording. I'll let you know the day it's out and send you the clips, quote cards and caption to share.

Rather meet in person? Happy to. If you prefer face to face, we can record in person. Taipei, Hsinchu, or somewhere else that suits you: we'll work out the place together. We cover the venue and all recording equipment. All you need to do is show up.

Prefer not to record? We can do it in writing: you answer by text, and I publish the exchange as an article on Substack and the Diverax website.

WHERE IT AIRS
  • YouTube

05

Off the table

  • Political positions and elections
  • Gossip and private life
  • Salaries, contracts and money
  • Gambling cases and legal disputes
  • Anything you tell me you'd rather skip

If a question comes up during recording that you'd rather not answer, just say "skip" and it stays out of the edit.

06

FAQ

Can I see the questions in advance?
Yes. Before we record, I send you three or four broad directions so you know where we're heading. I skip a question-by-question script so the conversation stays natural. If there's anything you'd rather avoid, just tell me.
What if I need to reschedule?
Just send me a message and we'll find another time. No problem at all.
Can I ask to cut something after recording?
Yes. Tell me which part after we record, and it stays out of the edit.
Is there a fee to be on the show?
None at all.

Up for a conversation?

Just send one time that works for you. I'll take care of the rest.
